column1: improvise§The engineer improvised a repair from a bicycle chain and a length of pipe, and it held for eleven years.§这位工程师用一根自行车链条和一截管子**临时凑出**了一个修补方案，它撑了十一年。§im-（不）+ provis（预见，同 provide 提供）→ 没预备就来
imprudent§It was imprudent to sign before the survey, and the crack in the foundation cost him the whole deposit.§勘察前就签字是**轻率的**，地基的那道裂缝让他赔上了全部押金。§im-（不）+ prudent（谨慎的）
impudent§His impudent question silenced the room and turned out to be the only one worth asking that evening.§他**放肆的**提问让全场安静下来，而它成了那晚唯一值得问的问题。§im-（不）+ pud（羞耻）
impugn§Nobody impugned her figures; they simply argued about what the figures were supposed to measure.§没有人**质疑**她的数字，人们只是争论这些数字本该测量什么。§im-（进入）+ pugn（打斗，同 pugnacious 好斗的）
impulsive§One impulsive purchase in 1987 became the most valuable object in the entire collection.§1987 年一次**冲动的**购买，成了整批藏品中最值钱的一件。§im-（进入）+ puls（推，同 pulse 脉搏）
impute§The report imputes the delay to the contractor, and the contractor's own file suggests four other causes.§报告把延误**归咎于**承包商，而承包商自己的卷宗提示了另外四个原因。§im-（进入）+ put（思量，同 compute 计算）
inaccessibility§The inaccessibility of the site protected it for four centuries and now keeps archaeologists away too.§这处遗址的**难以抵达**保护了它四个世纪，如今也把考古学家挡在了外面。§
inaccessible§The records are technically public and practically inaccessible: one reading room, open nine hours a week.§这些档案名义上公开，实际上**难以取用**——一间阅览室，每周开九小时。§in-（不）+ access（进入）
inaccurate§The figure was inaccurate by a factor of ten, and it appeared unchallenged in four government reports.§这个数字**误差**达十倍，却在四份政府报告里原样出现无人质疑。§
inadequacy§The inadequacy of the warning system was known in 1994 and documented again after every incident since.§预警系统的**不足**在 1994 年就已知晓，此后每次事故后又被记录一次。§
inadequate§Two nurses for forty beds is inadequate on a quiet night and dangerous on any other.§四十张床配两名护士，在安静的夜里**不够用**，在别的夜里则很危险。§in-（不）+ adequate（足够的）
inane§The questions were inane and the answers were careful, and the interview taught the audience nothing.§问题**空洞无物**而回答小心翼翼，这场访谈没让观众学到任何东西。§
inappropriate§The joke was inappropriate in the room he was in and would have been fine in almost any other.§这个玩笑在他所处的场合**不合时宜**，换到几乎任何别的场合都没问题。§
inapt§The comparison is inapt: one system serves nine million people and the other serves ninety thousand.§这个类比**不恰当**——一套系统服务九百万人，另一套服务九万人。§in-（不）+ apt（合适的）
inarticulate§He was inarticulate under pressure and devastating in writing, and the trial was conducted out loud.§他在压力下**语无伦次**，落笔却极具杀伤力，而审判是口头进行的。§in-（不）+ articulate（清晰表达）
inattention§A single moment's inattention at the level crossing cost the company nine months of interrupted production.§道口处仅仅片刻的**分神**，让公司损失了九个月的停产时间。§in-（不）+ attention（注意）
inaudible§Her reply was inaudible beyond the front row, and the microphone had been switched off for forty minutes.§她的回答在前排以外**听不见**，而话筒已经关了四十分钟。§in-（不）+ aud（听，同 audio 音频）
inauspicious§The beginning was inauspicious: two of the four founders left before the first product shipped.§开头**不吉利**——四位创始人中有两位在第一款产品出货前就走了。§
incandescent§She was incandescent about the decision and, in the letter she finally sent, entirely measured.§她对这个决定**怒火中烧**，而在最终寄出的信里则完全克制。§in-（进入）+ candesc（发白热，同 candle 蜡烛）
incantatory§The prose has an incantatory rhythm that carries readers past arguments they would otherwise question.§这些文字有一种**咒语般的**节奏，把读者带过了他们本会质疑的论证。§in-（进入）+ cant（唱，同 chant 吟诵）
incense§The tone of the refusal incensed people whom the refusal itself would not have troubled.§拒绝的语气**激怒**了那些本不会在意拒绝本身的人。§in-（进入）+ cens ← cand（燃烧）→ 点着火
inception§From its inception the programme was underfunded, and every review since has said so in the same words.§这个项目从**创立之初**就资金不足，此后每次评审都用同样的字眼这么说。§in-（进入）+ cept（拿，同 capture 捕获）→ 开头接手
incessant§The incessant noise from the plant made the nearest four streets almost impossible to sell houses in.§工厂**不间断的**噪音让最近的四条街几乎卖不出房子。§in-（不）+ cess（停止，同 cease 停止）
inchoate§The idea was inchoate in 1971 and recognizable, in a paper nobody cited, five years before that.§这个想法在 1971 年还**初具雏形**，而在五年前一篇无人引用的论文里已可辨认。§
incidental§The most valuable finding was incidental: they were looking for one mineral and found a fossil bed.§最有价值的发现是**附带的**——他们在找一种矿物，却找到了一处化石层。§in-（进入）+ cid（落下，同 accident 事故）
incisive§Her incisive question exposed in nine words what four hours of testimony had carefully avoided.§她**一针见血**的提问用九个字揭穿了四小时证词小心回避的东西。§in-（进入）+ cis（切，同 scissors 剪刀）
inclination§His inclination is always to wait, and on three of the four occasions that turned out to be right.§他的**倾向**永远是等待，而在四次里有三次证明这是对的。§in-（向）+ clin（倾斜，同 decline 下降）
inclusive§The figure is inclusive of tax, delivery, and installation, which is why it looks so much higher than the advertised price.§这个数字**含**税费、运费和安装费，所以看着比广告价高出许多。§in-（在内）+ clud（关闭，同 include 包括）
incoherence§The incoherence of the policy is not accidental: four departments wrote four sections and never met.§这项政策的**前后矛盾**并非偶然——四个部门写了四个部分，从未碰过头。§
incoherent§His account became incoherent after the fourth hour of questioning, which the court treated as evidence.§讯问到第四小时后他的陈述变得**语无伦次**，法庭把这当成了证据。§in-（不）+ co-（一起）+ her（黏，同 adhere 附着）
incompatible§The two accounts are incompatible, and one of the two witnesses must be mistaken about the time.§这两份陈述**互不相容**，两位证人中必有一位记错了时间。§in-（不）+ compatible（相容的）
incompetent§Calling the office incompetent is unfair: it has nine staff and the workload of about forty.§称这个办公室**无能**并不公平——它有九名员工，却承担约四十人的工作量。§in-（不）+ compet（胜任，同 compete 竞争）
incomprehensible§The instructions are incomprehensible to anyone who has not already done the job at least twice.§这些说明对没做过至少两次这项工作的人来说**无法理解**。§
inconclusive§Four studies were inconclusive, and the fifth found an effect that the first four had lacked the size to detect.§四项研究**未有定论**，第五项发现了一个前四项因规模不足而检测不到的效应。§
incongruity§The incongruity is what makes the photograph famous: a grand piano standing in a flooded field.§正是这种**不协调**让这张照片出名——一架三角钢琴立在被淹的田里。§in-（不）+ congru（一致，同 congruent 全等的）
incongruous§The modern wing looks incongruous from the street and, from inside, resolves the building's oldest problem.§这座现代侧翼从街上看**不协调**，从内部看却解决了这栋楼最老的问题。§
inconsequential§The change looked inconsequential and shifted about four million pounds from one budget to another.§这处改动看着**无关紧要**，却把约四百万英镑从一个预算挪到了另一个。§
inconsistency§The inconsistency runs through the whole file: the same event is dated three different ways.§这种**不一致**贯穿整个卷宗——同一件事被标上三种不同的日期。§
inconsistent§His evidence was inconsistent on the small details and unshakeable on the one that mattered.§他的证词在细枝末节上**前后不一**，在关键那一点上却毫不动摇。§
inconspicuous§The building is deliberately inconspicuous, and most people who pass it daily cannot say what it is.§这栋楼刻意**不引人注意**，每天路过的人多半说不出它是干什么的。§in-（不）+ conspicuous（显眼的）
incontrovertible§The evidence is incontrovertible on one point and silent on the four that the defence cares about.§证据在一点上**无可辩驳**，而在辩方关心的四点上则一无所言。§in-（不）+ contro（相对）+ vert（转）→ 无法翻转
incorporate§They incorporated the objection into the final draft and, in doing so, quietly reversed its meaning.§他们把这条异议**纳入**终稿，而这样做时悄悄颠倒了它的意思。§in-（进入）+ corpor（身体，同 corporation 法人）
incorrigible§He is an incorrigible optimist, which has cost him money four times and saved the company twice.§他是个**积习难改的**乐观主义者，这让他赔过四次钱，也救过公司两次。§in-（不）+ corrig（纠正，同 correct 正确的）
incorruptible§The one incorruptible inspector in the district was transferred four times in nine years.§全区唯一**廉洁不阿的**检查员九年里被调动了四次。§
incredulous§The committee was incredulous until the technician repeated the demonstration with their own equipment.§委员会**满腹狐疑**，直到技师用他们自己的设备重做了一遍演示。§in-（不）+ cred（相信，同 credit 信用）
incubate§The idea incubated for nine years in a drawer and was written in eleven weeks once she finally started.§这个想法在抽屉里**孵化**了九年，等她真动笔时十一周就写完了。§in-（在内）+ cub（躺，同 incumbent 在职的）→ 伏着孵
indebted§The town remains indebted to a benefactor whose name appears on nothing he actually paid for.§这座小镇仍然**感念**一位恩人，而他实际出资的一切上面都没有他的名字。§
indecent§The delay was indecent rather than illegal: eleven months to answer a letter about a dying man.§这次拖延是**不体面**而非违法的——用十一个月回复一封关于垂危病人的信。§in-（不）+ decent（得体的）
indecision§Indecision cost more than either option would have: the price rose forty percent while the committee met.§**优柔寡断**的代价超过任何一个选项——委员会开会期间价格上涨了四成。§
indecisive§The result was indecisive, and both sides declared victory within an hour of the count.§结果**难分胜负**，计票结束一小时内双方都宣布获胜。§
indecorous§It would be indecorous to name him here, and everyone in the room already knew exactly who was meant.§在这里点他的名是**不合礼数的**，而在场每个人都已清楚说的是谁。§in-（不）+ decor（合宜，同 decorate 装饰）
indefatigable§The indefatigable volunteer catalogued nine thousand items in four years and asked for nothing at all.§这位**不知疲倦的**志愿者四年编目九千件物品，什么也没要过。§in-（不）+ de-（去）+ fatig（疲劳，同 fatigue 疲劳）
indefensible§The position is indefensible on the evidence, which is why the argument has moved to procedure instead.§从证据看这个立场**站不住脚**，所以争论转到了程序上。§
indefinite§The suspension was indefinite, and four years later nobody could say who had the power to end it.§停职是**无限期的**，四年后没人说得出谁有权结束它。§in-（不）+ definite（明确的）
indelible§The impression was indelible: forty years later he could still describe the room and what was on the table.§这个印象**难以磨灭**——四十年后他仍能描述那个房间和桌上的东西。§in-（不）+ del（删除，同 delete 删除）
indeterminate§The date is indeterminate: the style suggests one century and the materials suggest another entirely.§年代**无法确定**——风格指向一个世纪，材料指向另一个完全不同的世纪。§
indictment§The indictment ran to four hundred counts, and the trial that followed lasted nineteen months.§这份**起诉书**列了四百项罪名，随后的审判持续了十九个月。§in-（向）+ dict（说，同 dictate 口述）→ 当众宣告罪名
indifference§Indifference did more damage than opposition: the proposal simply sat unread for eleven months.§**漠不关心**造成的损害超过反对——这项提案就那样无人翻阅地搁了十一个月。§
indigence§The indigence of the parish was recorded in 1841, and the same four streets are still the poorest today.§这个教区的**贫困**在 1841 年就有记载，同样那四条街至今仍是最穷的。§indig（缺乏）
indigenous§The indigenous variety yields less and survives drought that kills every imported strain in the field.§**本土的**品种产量较低，却能挺过杀死田里所有引进品系的干旱。§indi-（在内）+ gen（出生，同 genus 属）
indignant§She was indignant on behalf of people who had been told, four times, that nothing could be done.§她为那些被告知四次「无能为力」的人感到**愤慨**。§in-（不）+ dign（有价值，同 dignity 尊严）→ 觉得被贬低
indiscernible§The difference is indiscernible to the eye and obvious on any instrument made after 1970.§这个差别肉眼**难以分辨**，在 1970 年后造的任何仪器上都一目了然。§
indiscretion§One indiscretion in a hotel bar ended a career that four decades of careful work had built.§酒店酒吧里的一次**失言**，终结了四十年谨慎经营建立的事业。§in-（不）+ discretion（谨慎）
indiscriminate§The cuts were indiscriminate, and the department that had come in under budget lost as much as the others.§削减是**不加区分的**，那个预算有结余的部门损失得和其他部门一样多。§in-（不）+ discriminate（区分）
indisputable§One fact is indisputable and the rest is argument: the money left the account on a Tuesday.§有一个事实**无可争辩**，其余都是论辩——钱是在一个周二离开账户的。§in-（不）+ dispute（争论）
